title: Proposed Element : Message

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve? Email clients and other places where messages are used often have a lot of content on the page * general site landmarks, header, folder, nav, etc. * Inbox and folders listing other messages * Controls for the message, replying, delete, archive, mark as spam, etc. * Advertising banners * Other admin tools, calendar, video chat, etc. The message is mostly displayed in the flow of the HTML document rather than using an iframe. When using a screen reader it can take time to find the messages and it can be hard to identify the exact start and end of the message. This makes me believe that it’s important to clearly wrap these messages in appropriate markup to improve the accessible user experience. I’m approaching this from the point of view of email as that is what I know but I think there are a range of uses. * Email * Social media direct messages * Notification messages (when served in a notification inbox rather than a dialog modal) * Comments * Messenger apps ### What solutions exist today? The `
` element is a good candidate to do this job and I believe it covers everything I’m looking for, however I feel the naming often confuses people. Whenever I talk to developers about it I always need to explain that this is using article in its meaning of an item, and not just for blog posts. I don’t know how screen reader users feel about this but I feel like they may also be confused by it, that assumption needs some proper research to see if this an issue or not. When the word _"article"_ is translated by the user-agent/screen reader into differently languages the ambiguity may be less(or more). I'd be particularly interested in how languages not based on Latin handle it. Because of the ambiguity of the naming I've been tempted into using `aria-roledescription` to give the element a more user friendly name. But it feels a little dirty and wrong. ### How would you solve it? Create a new `` element. Essentially this would be very similar to the `
` element but with more specific naming. I'm thinking a message may look something like this ```html

Hi everyone, I'm thinking about a new HTML element

Mark Robbins mark@example.com

17th October 16.30
Hi everyone, I'm just wondering if we could maybe use a new HTML element to define a messages in an HTML document. It's a very common use case across the web but it's not implemented very consistently. Thanks, Mark ``` And a reply to that message may look like this, with the original email included in a nested `` element. ```html

RE: Hi everyone, I'm thinking about a new HTML element

Rark Mobbins Rark@example.com

17th October 17.30
Hi Mark, Yeah that sounds like fun. Cheers, Rark
-- Original message --
From Mark Robbins Mark@example.com
Send 17th October 16.30
Hi everyone, I'm thinking about a new HTML element
Hi everyone, I'm just wondering if we could maybe use a new HTML element to define a messages in an HTML doucment. It's a very common use case across the web but it's not implemented very consistently. Thanks, Mark ``` ### Anything else? Looking at how popular email clients handle message layouts today * Gmail, Yahoo, AOL webmail all use `role="listitem"` * Outlook webmail uses `role="document"` Looking at some other apps * Facebook messenger uses `role="gridcell"` * Twitter uses `role="button"`
